title: Conditional field-extension invariance across a dense open
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a reduced curve [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, $r$ a prime, and $F$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] with $r\,\mathrm{id}_F=0$. For any dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ let $G=j_!j^*F$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. The conditional assertion $C_6(X,F)$ is equivalent to $C_6(X,G)$ and $C_7(X,F)$ is equivalent to $C_7(X,G)$ [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. Here $C_6$ asks for bijectivity of every canonical cohomology pullback in every degree under invertible-order torsion, and $C_7$ asks for those same bijections under properness, for all cartesian squares of algebraically closed field extension [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback]. The maps are the original cohomologyMap of the underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof: the five-term exact sequence and remark (c)

proof.text: Let Z be the reduced closed complement of U. Finite type makes X Noetherian with finitely many irreducible components. Density and openness put the generic point of every component in U: if its closure meets U, every generalization of that point of intersection lies in U. Thus no irreducible component lies in Z. Any strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets in Z would extend by a component of X to a chain of length at least two in X, contradicting dimension at most one. Hence Z has dimension at most zero. Its underlying space is finite and discrete, and each residue field is k. The same argument applies to any open immersion W into X and the complement W times_X Z.

The open-closed short exact sequence of module sheaves is 0 -> G -> F -> i_*i^*F -> 0, with the first arrow the specified adjunction counit. Forgetting module structure gives a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves. Finite exact direct image and the Leray identification give H^q(X,i_*i^*F)=H^q(Z,i^*F). This vanishes for q>0. Inverse image along any open immersion is exact and computes the analogous closed direct image over the intersection with Z.

For a cartesian square of algebraically closed field extension, inverse image identifies each new geometric stalk on the closed complement with its original stalk. The degree-zero pullback of the closed term is the corresponding product map and is bijective; the positive-degree maps are between zero groups. Use the global-sections pullback theorem in dimension zero for degree zero and zero-dimensional cohomology for the other degrees. Leray and finite exact direct image identify these with the maps for B=i_*i^*F.

The pullback-cohomology ladder has canonical cohomologyMap vertical arrows. Its higher-degree counit maps are bijective over both fields. Its low-degree part is 0 -> H^0(G) -> H^0(F) -> H^0(B) -> H^1(G) -> H^1(F) -> 0. When all vertical maps for G are bijective, apply the five lemma at H^0(F) and H^1(F). Conversely, when those for F are bijective, apply it at H^0(G) and H^1(G). The known B and zero end maps supply the remaining isomorphisms. This proves that the simultaneous comparison bijections for all degrees transfer in both directions.

This proves the conditional proper assertion. For the invertible-order assertion, the stalks of G are those of F on U and zero outside it; both are r-torsion. If r is invertible in k, both have invertible-order torsion and use the ladder. If r is the positive characteristic, an invertible-order hypothesis on either sheaf forces it to be zero, by coprimality of its stalk annihilators; both that sheaf and its pullback have zero cohomology. Thus the conditional implications hold even when the invertible-order predicates themselves are different.

theorem dense_open_base_change (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [IsReduced X]
    (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime] (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    [Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf F] (hF : r • 𝟙 F = 0)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set X)) :
    let G := (U.ι)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj
      ((U.ι)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj F)
    (BaseChangeOfInvertibleOrder Λ f F ↔ BaseChangeOfInvertibleOrder Λ f G) ∧
    (BaseChangeOfIsProper Λ f F ↔ BaseChangeOfIsProper Λ f G)
